chunks: From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever says to his companion, ‘May you have no father, and may you have no mother,’ then let him give something in charity. And whoever says, ‘No, by my father,’ then let him say, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,’ for indeed that is an expiation for his statement.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; a formula of tawhid recited as expiation here
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: with something; indicating even a small charitable offering
key_terms.فَلْيَتَصَدَّقْ: then let him give charity; an act of expiation through charitable giving
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: expiation; that which wipes away the fault of the utterance
key_terms.لَا وَأَبِي: no, by my father; a prohibited or blameworthy form of oath-like speech
key_terms.لِصَاحِبِهِ: to his companion; indicating the social context of speech between people

ai.seo_question: What expiation is prescribed for saying offensive words or swearing by one's father in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that improper or blameworthy speech should be followed by an act of expiation. It prescribes charity for insulting expressions and the shahadah for an oath-like expression invoking one's father, showing moral and legal concern for disciplining the tongue.
